summary.headline: Three more labs accept government safety tests — Conquerors falls
summary.body: The safety story firmed up. Microsoft, Google DeepMind and xAI agreed to give NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation early access to frontier models for national-security testing, joining OpenAI and Anthropic. Real outside checks strengthen Alignment & Control, which lifts Protector God and Gatekeeper and pushes Conquerors and Zookeeper down. The jobs picture darkened: Coinbase cut about 700 roles and PayPal plans to cut about 20% of staff over two to three years, both citing AI. That weakens Shared Prosperity. Major publishers also sued Meta over training Llama on pirated books, adding to Tech Backlash and Reversion. Horizon Balance rose to +2.09, up 0.68, the best day of the period.
summary.movers_note: Protector God +0.6, Conquerors -0.6 and Gatekeeper +0.5, all mainly from the NIST pre-release testing agreements (+0.56, -0.56 and +0.48).

events.title: Microsoft, Google and xAI agree to pre-release US government security testing
events.summary: NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation will get early access to frontier models from Microsoft, Google DeepMind and xAI for national-security testing, joining OpenAI and Anthropic.
events.reason: Expands third-party (government) pre-deployment eval regime to most US frontier labs.

events.title: Coinbase cuts ~700 jobs (14%) to rebuild around AI
events.summary: Coinbase announced about 700 layoffs as CEO Brian Armstrong restructured the company around AI agents and consolidated roles.

events.title: PayPal to cut ~20% of staff over 2-3 years in AI-driven turnaround
events.summary: WSJ reported PayPal plans to cut roughly 4,760 jobs; executives said on the earnings call they will aggressively adopt AI and automation for $1.5B savings.
events.reason: Large planned cut tied to AI, multi-year and not fully confirmed.

events.title: Major publishers file class action against Meta over AI training on pirated books
events.summary: Elsevier, Hachette, McGraw Hill and others sued Meta alleging Llama was trained on pirated copyrighted works; Meta says training is fair use.
events.reason: Creative-industry legal pushback against AI training.
